name: Weight Wave
desc: A word whose letters breathe from hairline to black as a wave rolls through them. Hover it and the crest follows your pointer.
prompt: Build a kinetic headline: the word MOTION in a condensed variable display font (Big Shoulders Display, weight axis 100–900), uppercase, huge, centered on a soft neutral background. Split it into letter spans. A sine wave travels left to right through the letters and drives each letter's weight between 100 and 900, so the word looks like it inhales and exhales. When the pointer is over the word, the crest locks to the pointer: letters near it go black, letters further away go hairline, using a smoothstep falloff. Every letter eases toward its target weight (lerp about 0.12 per frame) so nothing snaps, and letter-spacing tightens slightly as weight rises so the word doesn't jitter in width. Light and dark themes via prefers-color-scheme. Single HTML file, no libraries.

name: Scramble Decode
desc: Words resolve out of random glyphs, letter by letter, like a terminal cracking a code. Click for the next word.
prompt: Make a 'scramble decode' text effect in a monospace font (JetBrains Mono), large and centered. The word cycles through DECODE, SIGNAL, PAYLOAD, UNLOCK, RUNTIME. To change word, each character position starts scrambling at a staggered frame (about 3 frames apart, left to right, with a little randomness), shows random glyphs from A–Z, 0–9 and symbols like #%&*+=<>/ for 10–24 frames at ~30 fps, then locks to the target letter. Scrambling glyphs are in the accent color, about a third of them dimmed; locked letters are in the ink color. Pad words to equal length so the layout never jumps. Click or press Enter to decode the next word, and autoplay every ~1.7 s otherwise. Expose the final word with aria-label. Light and dark themes. Single HTML file.

name: Split-Flap Board
desc: A departures-board word that clatters through the alphabet, flap by flap, until every tile lands. Click to change the status.
prompt: Build an airport split-flap display with 8 tiles in a dark rounded housing. Each tile is split into a top and bottom half with a thin seam. To change a character, a tile steps through the character set ' ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ0123456789:' one flap at a time: the top flap (showing the old character) rotates down on rotateX from 0 to -90deg with ease-in and darkens, then the bottom flap (showing the new character) swings from 90deg to 0 with ease-out, about 45 ms each. The static top half already shows the next character, the static bottom half shows the old one until the flap lands. Tiles start 40 ms apart, left to right. Cycle through BOARDING, DELAYED, ON TIME, GATE 12, LANDED; click to advance. Bold monospace characters in off-white on charcoal tiles, perspective on each tile, Web Animations API. Single HTML file.

name: Typewriter Loop
desc: A terminal prompt that types, pauses, deletes and moves on, with a block caret that only blinks when it's idle. Start typing to take over.
prompt: Build a typewriter loop in a big monospace font: a muted '>' prompt, then text, then a solid block caret in the accent color. It types each phrase in turn ('type.', 'delete.', 'repeat.', 'ship it.', 'make it move.') with human-feeling jitter (50–130 ms per character, a longer beat after punctuation), holds for 1.4 s, then deletes at double speed and starts the next one. The caret is solid while typing or deleting and blinks with steps(1) only while idle. If the user presses keys, the loop stops and their keystrokes type into the line instead (Backspace deletes, max 18 characters); after 6 s of no input the loop resumes. Announce changes politely to screen readers. Light and dark themes. Single HTML file.

name: Bar Wipe Reveal
desc: Three lines of a headline revealed by solid colour bars that wipe in, uncover the word and wipe out the other side, staggered line by line.
prompt: Build a bar-wipe headline reveal: three stacked uppercase lines (MAKE / THINGS / MOVE) in a heavy condensed display font, left-aligned. Each line has a solid bar the size of the line: bar 1 in the accent blue, bar 2 in a warm yellow, bar 3 in the ink color. Reveal: each bar scales in from the left (scaleX 0→1, 380 ms, expo-out), the word appears underneath at that moment with a small rise, then the bar scales out to the right (transform-origin right, 420 ms). Lines start 140 ms apart. Hide is the mirror image (bars come in from the right, word disappears, bars leave to the left). Loop reveal → hold 1.6 s → hide → pause; click replays. Use the Web Animations API and only transforms and opacity. Light and dark themes. Single HTML file.

name: Extruded Word
desc: A slab of solid type with a deep extrusion that swings to stay behind the face as the word tilts toward your pointer.
prompt: Make a 3D extruded word: DEPTH in a heavy condensed display font, very large, face in a warm yellow. Build the extrusion from ~18 stacked text-shadows, each 1 step further back, colored from the accent blue fading toward black (color-mix in oklab), plus one soft blurred shadow at the end. The word tilts with rotateX/rotateY (max ±18°) toward the pointer, easing at 0.08 per frame; with no pointer it drifts on a slow Lissajous path. Recompute the shadow offsets every frame from the tilt so the extrusion always sits on the far side of the face, as if it were a real block of type. Perspective 900px on the page. Light and dark themes. Single HTML file, no libraries.

name: Gooey Liquid Toggle
desc: A switch whose knob stretches like a drop of liquid, leaving a trail that pulls back into it as it lands.
prompt: Build a liquid toggle switch: a 132×64 pill track that is grey when off and accent blue when on. Inside, a white 48px knob plus two smaller trailing blobs (40px and 32px) sit inside a container with an SVG goo filter (feGaussianBlur stdDeviation 6, then a feColorMatrix alpha of 22/-10, composited atop the source), so they merge into one liquid shape. On toggle the knob moves 68px with a springy cubic-bezier(.34,1.56,.64,1) over 550 ms, and the trailing blobs follow with 70 ms and 150 ms delays on an ease-out curve, so the knob stretches into a drop and the tail snaps back into it. Use a real button with role=switch and aria-checked, keyboard and click. Under it, a small monospace status label crossfades between 'liquid: off' and 'liquid: on'. Autoplay toggles every 1.4 s until the user clicks. Light and dark themes. Single HTML file.

name: Magnetic Button
desc: A call-to-action that leans toward the pointer as it gets close, its label moving a little further than the button for depth. Clicks ripple from where you pressed.
prompt: Build a magnetic CTA button: a large pill 'Get started →' in ink color with background-colored text. Within a 180px radius of the button center, the button translates toward the pointer by 35% of the offset scaled by proximity, and its inner label moves an extra 18% for a parallax feel; both follow with a lerp of 0.15 per frame and spring back to rest when the pointer leaves. On press, scale to 0.96, spawn a circular accent ripple from the exact click point that expands and fades, and swap the label to '✓ On it' for a second. When nobody is interacting, a small demo cursor dot drifts around on a Lissajous path so the effect plays by itself; hide it as soon as a real pointer moves. Light and dark themes. Single HTML file.

name: Async Action Button
desc: A submit button that collapses into a spinner while it works, then opens into a green 'Sent' with a drawn check, or a red 'Try again' with a shake.
prompt: Build an async action button with four states. Idle: a 200×56 accent pill reading 'Send invite' with a paper-plane icon. Loading: the pill's width animates to a 56px circle (450 ms, expo-out) and the label slides up and out while a white ring spinner slides in. Success: the button widens to 150px, turns green, and shows 'Sent' with a checkmark whose stroke draws in via stroke-dashoffset. Error: widens to 170px, turns red, shows 'Try again' and shakes horizontally for 420 ms. After 1.6 s it returns to idle. All labels are absolutely stacked layers that crossfade with a small vertical slide. Clicks during work are ignored. Announce each state in an aria-live region. Demo loop: success, success, error. Text on the accent must stay readable in both light and dark themes. Single HTML file.

name: Like Burst
desc: A heart that pops, throws a ring and a spray of confetti dots, while the counter rolls to its new number.
prompt: Build a like button: an outlined heart icon next to a count (1,204) in a pill. On like, the heart fills with a coral red and scales 0.6 → 1.25 → 1 on a spring, a thin ring expands from behind it and fades, and 12 small dots in red, yellow and blue burst outward in a circle at slightly randomized distances and fade, using the Web Animations API. The count rolls: the old number slides up and fades out while the new one slides in from below. Unlike reverses the fill with a quick shrink and rolls the number down, no particles. Use aria-pressed. Demo toggles every ~1.6 s until clicked. Light and dark themes. Single HTML file.

name: Spring Stepper
desc: A − / + quantity stepper whose digits roll in the direction you count, overshooting slightly, and that shakes when you hit a limit. Hold a button to repeat.
prompt: Build a quantity stepper: a rounded group with a '−' button, a large tabular number, and a '+' button. Changing the value rolls the digits: going up, the old number exits upward and the new one enters from below with a springy overshoot (cubic-bezier(.34,1.56,.64,1), 420 ms); going down, the reverse. Range 0–12. At a limit the whole control does a short horizontal shake and the blocked button flashes. Holding a button repeats every 110 ms after a 380 ms delay (pointer and keyboard). Buttons scale to 0.9 on press. Arrow keys work when the control is focused. Expose the value with role=spinbutton and aria-valuenow/min/max. Demo does a random walk of steps. Light and dark themes. Single HTML file.

name: Hold to Confirm
desc: A destructive button that has to be held down. A red fill sweeps across, inverting the label as it goes, and drains away if you let go early.
prompt: Build a press-and-hold confirm button for a destructive action: an outlined 240×58 pill reading 'Hold to delete' with a trash icon. While pressed (pointer, Space or Enter), a red fill grows left to right over 1.1 s; the label is duplicated inside the fill in white and revealed with clip-path inset so the text inverts exactly at the fill edge. Releasing early drains the fill back at three times the speed. When it reaches 100%, the button settles into a solid red 'Deleted' state with a drawn check, and a slight scale pop, then resets after 1.6 s. Show a small hint below ('press and hold') that changes to 'keep holding…' while held. Demo: one early release, then a full hold. Light and dark themes. Single HTML file.

name: Floating Label Field
desc: An email field whose label lifts and shrinks out of the way, with an underline that draws from the centre and a check that pops in once the address is valid.
prompt: Build a floating-label email field. The label sits inside the empty field like a placeholder; on focus or when filled it moves up and scales to 0.78 (transform only, 250 ms ease-out) and takes the accent color. A 2px accent underline draws outward from the center (scaleX 0→1) on focus over a neutral 1px base line. When the value is a valid email a green check icon pops in on the right with a spring scale; if the field is left non-empty and invalid, the underline and label turn red and a helper line below swaps from 'We'll never share it.' to 'That doesn't look like an email.' with a short slide. Use :placeholder-shown with placeholder=' ' so the float works without JS; JS only handles validity classes. Demo types 'phil@studio' then completes to 'phil@studio.dev' letter by letter, then clears. Light and dark themes. Single HTML file.

name: Sliding Segmented Control
desc: Day / Week / Month / Year tabs with a pill that springs between them, driving a little bar chart that regrows on every switch.
prompt: Build a segmented control with four options (Day, Week, Month, Year) in a rounded chip-colored track. A surface-colored pill with a soft shadow sits behind the active option and moves by animating left and width with an overshooting spring curve (cubic-bezier(.34,1.56,.64,1), 480 ms). The active label goes to ink color, the rest are muted. Under it, a card with 12 bars whose heights change per option: bars regrow with a 25 ms stagger, and a big total number above them counts to its new value. Use role=tablist/tab with aria-selected, roving tabindex, and Left/Right arrow keys. Demo cycles through options every 1.6 s until the user interacts. Light and dark themes. Single HTML file.

name: One-Time Code
desc: Six code boxes that pop as digits land, shake red on a wrong code and ripple green, box by box, when it's right. Paste works too.
prompt: Build a 6-digit one-time-code input: six square boxes with large tabular digits. Typing a digit pops the box (scale 1 → 1.08 → 1) and moves focus to the next; Backspace clears and moves back; arrow keys move; pasting a 6-digit code fills all boxes. The focused box has an accent ring. When all six are filled, verify: the correct code (246810) turns the boxes green one by one with a 60 ms stagger and a small upward hop, then shows 'Verified' with a check; a wrong code turns them red, shakes the row, then clears and refocuses the first box. Use inputmode=numeric, autocomplete=one-time-code, aria-labels per digit and a live region for the result. Show a muted hint 'demo code: 246810'. Demo enters a wrong code, then the right one. Light and dark themes. Single HTML file.

name: Tilting Value Slider
desc: A range slider whose value bubble swings like it's hanging from the thumb: drag fast and it tilts against the motion, then settles.
prompt: Build a custom range slider (0–100) for 'Volume'. A 6px rounded track with an accent fill, a 26px white thumb with a soft shadow that grows on hover/drag, and a value bubble above the thumb (a rounded chip with a small pointer) showing the number. The bubble behaves like it hangs from the thumb: compute the thumb's velocity each frame and tilt the bubble against it (rotate up to ±28°, transform-origin at the bottom), then spring back to upright with a damped spring. The bubble scales up while dragging. Drag with pointer capture anywhere on the track, Left/Right/Home/End keys, role=slider with aria-valuenow. Demo glides the value between random targets with ease-in-out when idle. Light and dark themes. Single HTML file.

name: Password Strength
desc: A password field with a four-segment meter that fills and changes colour as rules tick off below, each with a drawn check.
prompt: Build a password field with a strength meter. Under the input, four rounded segments fill left to right as the score rises (0–4), each segment growing with scaleX and a 40 ms stagger; the colour shifts red → amber → green → accent as the password gets stronger, with a label on the right (Too weak / Okay / Strong / Excellent) that crossfades. Below, a checklist of rules (8+ characters, an uppercase letter, a number, a symbol); when a rule is met its circle fills and a check draws in with stroke-dashoffset, and the text goes from muted to ink. Score = rules met, plus a bonus at 14+ characters, capped at 4. Include a show/hide eye button with aria-pressed. Demo types 'sunset', then 'Sunset42!', then 'Sunset42!harbour' and clears. Light and dark themes. Single HTML file.

name: Drawn Checklist
desc: Checkboxes that draw their tick with a pen stroke while a line strikes through the task, and a progress bar fills along the top.
prompt: Build a to-do checklist card titled 'Render day' with a small progress bar and an 'x of 3' counter. Each row is a real checkbox (visually hidden) with a custom 24px rounded box. Checking it fills the box with the accent, draws the tick with stroke-dashoffset (300 ms, ease-out), pops the box slightly on a spring, and draws a 2px strike line across the task text from left to right (scaleX) as the text fades to muted. Unchecking reverses it, quicker. The progress bar width eases to the share of done tasks. Tasks: 'Storyboard the beats', 'Render the 4K master', 'Mix to −14 LUFS'. Keyboard works natively. Demo checks the tasks one by one, then clears them. Light and dark themes. Single HTML file.

name: Orbital Loader
desc: Three dashed orbits with dots that speed up and coast around a breathing core, with a monospace status line cycling underneath. CSS only.
prompt: Build a CSS-only orbital loader. Three concentric dashed rings (70, 110 and 150px) in the line color. Ring 1 carries two accent dots, ring 2 carries three yellow dots and spins the opposite way, ring 3 carries one ink dot. Each ring rotates with an ease-in-out cubic-bezier(.65,0,.35,1) so the dots accelerate and coast instead of spinning at constant speed, with durations of 1.6 s, 2.4 s and 3.2 s. In the middle, an accent core that breathes (scale 0.8 ↔ 1 with a soft glow). Under it, a monospace line 'fetching orbital-dots' whose trailing dots animate with steps(). Wrap it in role=status with an aria-label. Respect prefers-reduced-motion by slowing everything to a gentle pulse. Light and dark themes. Single HTML file, no JavaScript.

name: Countdown Ring
desc: A ten-second ring timer: the arc drains smoothly, digits roll each second, the last three seconds turn red and pulse, and zero bursts into 'Go'.
prompt: Build a circular countdown timer. An SVG ring (r=70, 10px stroke, round caps) in the accent color over a faint track drains smoothly from full to empty over 10 s via stroke-dashoffset, driven by requestAnimationFrame so it never steps. The remaining whole seconds sit in the middle in a big condensed display font; when the number changes it rolls (old slides up and fades, new rises from below on a spring). In the last 3 seconds the ring and digits turn red and the ring pulses once per second. At zero, show 'GO' with a scale pop and a ring that bursts outward and fades, hold 1.2 s, then restart. Click the timer to restart early. Use role=timer with aria-live updates only on whole seconds. Light and dark themes. Single HTML file.

name: Stacking Toasts
desc: Notifications that pile up as a neat deck, the newest in front. Hover the stack and it fans out into a list; each toast leaves on its own timer.
prompt: Build a stacking toast system anchored bottom-center. Each toast is a 320px surface card with an icon in a tinted circle (success green, info blue, upload yellow), a title, a muted line and a close button. New toasts enter from below (translateY 100% → 0, opacity 0 → 1, spring). Collapsed, the stack looks like a deck: toast i sits at translateY(-i·14px) scale(1 - i·0.05), toasts beyond the third fade out. Hovering or focusing the stack expands it into a list where each toast moves up by the cumulative height of the ones in front plus 10px gaps; all positions transition with cubic-bezier(.22,1,.36,1) over 400 ms. Each toast auto-dismisses after 4.5 s (timers pause while expanded) and exits by sliding down and fading. A 'Show toast' button at the top adds one. Use role=status/aria-live=polite. Demo pushes a toast every 1.5 s. Light and dark themes. Single HTML file.

name: Skeleton to Content
desc: A loading card made of shimmering placeholder blocks that hand over to the real content piece by piece, without a single layout jump.
prompt: Build a skeleton-loading card that hands over to real content. The card has a 16:9 media area, a 40px avatar with name and time, a title, and two lines of text. In the loading state each piece is a chip-coloured rounded block with a diagonal shimmer gradient sweeping across all blocks in sync (background-attachment: fixed so the shine lines up). The skeleton blocks are the exact size of the content they stand for. When loaded, each piece crossfades from its block to the real content with a 70 ms stagger (media first, then avatar, name, title, text), with a tiny 4px rise; the media is a CSS gradient 'video still' with a play button. Toggle with a 'Reload' button; demo loops loading 1.8 s → loaded 2.6 s. Use aria-busy on the card. Light and dark themes. Single HTML file.

name: Copy Command
desc: An install command with a copy button whose two-sheet icon folds into a tick, while a 'Copied' tag hops up above it.
prompt: Build a copy-command chip: a dark monospace pill showing '$ npm install motion' with a square copy button on the right. The icon is two overlapping rounded rectangles. On click, copy the command with navigator.clipboard, then morph the icon: both rectangles scale down and fade out (200 ms) while a check stroke draws in with stroke-dashoffset and the button background tints green; a small 'Copied!' tag pops up above the button (translateY 6px → 0, scale .8 → 1 on a spring) and fades out after 1.4 s, when the icon morphs back. Announce 'Copied to clipboard' via aria-live. Demo clicks every 2.6 s (visual only, no clipboard write) until the user interacts. Light and dark themes (the chip stays dark in both). Single HTML file.

name: Ringing Bell
desc: A notification bell that swings from its hook, clapper lagging behind, as the badge pops and counts up. Click to clear and the badge shrinks away.
prompt: Build a notification bell button. The bell is an SVG with the body and the clapper as separate parts. When a notification arrives, the body swings from a pivot at its top (rotate 0 → 16° → −14° → 10° → −6° → 3° → 0 over 800 ms) and the clapper swings the opposite way with a slight delay, so it looks physical. A red badge at the top right pops in (scale 0 → 1.3 → 1, spring) on the first notification and, for later ones, bumps and rolls its number upward. Clicking the bell clears: the badge shrinks to 0 and the aria-label updates ('Notifications, 3 unread' → 'Notifications'). Demo: three arrivals 1.8 s apart, then a clear. Light and dark themes. Single HTML file.
